threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop instead of knowing to just walk a minute to catch the 38 at the next one.
Last night on the N133, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 'Wonderwall'—drunk, probably, but I think he had a better voice than some pros.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a busker near Hermannplatz mixing rap with the sound of a nearby tram; that blend of chaos felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a doner, sip a craft beer, and catch a spontaneous tandem bicycle race on a Tuesday afternoon. It's pure chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the real way to get a burrito at La Taqueria is to order it 'dine-in' to avoid the wait at peak hours.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with a ukulele as we waited for a delayed bus. Classic Civic Center vibe—only in SF do delays come with live music.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and hype, but it’s the little plazas and the locals with their cats that make it home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they order coffee—always asking for milk when a late is a better fit in this heat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You think the 106 bus runs on time because you saw one arrive at 10:03. Welcome to Stoke Newington. It’s a game of patience.
Caught a night bus from Croydon the other week. A couple of blokes were loudly debating if a kebab counts as breakfast. Only in South London!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a pigeon steal a bratwurst from a tourist's hand at Tempelhofer Feld. Classic Neukölln, where even the birds know how to hustle.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand that opens at 3 AM on weekends, serving late-night revelers their greasy fix with a side of Berliner charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their patience at Muni delays—everyone else freaks out when the bus is late, but we just know to grab a pupusa nearby.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy carrying a cat in a backpack on the 5-Fulton today, completely unfazed. Only in SF do we normalize that while dodging delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut in the late afternoon sun.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll catch them ordering a 'café con leche' at 5 PM like it's breakfast time, oblivious to the local rhythm.
